notes: All index_0_100 fields are Travelomore editorial indices calibrated on a fixed rubric (see docs/normalization_rules.md §4). Physical measures (km, hours, °C, ₹, µg/m³) are observed or market-sampled. Every city inherits unspecified signals from country:TH.

entities.name: Bangkok
entities.summary: The country's gateway and its most complete city: temples and palaces by day, rooftop bars and night markets after dark, world-class private hospitals, a metro that actually works, and the cheapest luxury-to-price ratio in the region.

entities.name: Pattaya
entities.summary: A two-hour drive from Bangkok airport and the default nightlife add-on for Indian groups. Walking Street and the cabaret circuit dominate; the beaches are mediocre but Jomtien and the offshore islands soften it for families.

entities.name: Phuket
entities.summary: Thailand's most complete island: direct flights from India, a JCI hospital, five-star resorts, Patong's nightlife, Phi Phi/James Bond day trips, and beaches that range from party-loud to family-calm depending on which coast you pick.

entities.name: Krabi (Ao Nang / Railay)
entities.summary: Limestone karsts, longtail boats and the four-island circuit. Calmer and cheaper than Phuket, with world-class rock climbing at Railay and easy access to Phi Phi — but thinner medical cover and boat-dependent access to the best beaches.

entities.name: Koh Phi Phi
entities.summary: The postcard island — Maya Bay, viewpoint sunsets, and a village that turns into a beach-party strip after dark. No cars, no hospital, boat-only access: spectacular for young groups, structurally hostile to strollers, wheelchairs and medical risk.

entities.name: Koh Samui
entities.summary: The Gulf's polished resort island — an airport on the island itself, a Bangkok Hospital branch, luxury villas, and a monsoon calendar that runs opposite to Phuket. The safest island pick for families, seniors and honeymooners.

entities.name: Koh Phangan
entities.summary: Full Moon Party island. Two personalities: Haad Rin's monthly beach rave, and a quiet yoga/wellness north coast. Boat-only access, minimal medical cover, and a party calendar that dictates pricing and crowding.

entities.name: Koh Tao
entities.summary: The cheapest place on earth to get PADI-certified, and the reason most divers come to Thailand. Small, hilly, boat-only, and thin on medical infrastructure — with a decompression chamber but no real hospital.

entities.name: Chiang Mai
entities.summary: The cultural capital of the north: a walled old town of 300 temples, ethical elephant sanctuaries, the best coworking scene in Asia, and cool-season weather. The one hard caveat is the Feb-Apr burning season, when PM2.5 goes off the scale.

entities.name: Chiang Rai
entities.summary: Quieter, cooler and stranger than Chiang Mai — the White Temple, the Blue Temple, hill-tribe villages and the Golden Triangle. Extremely photogenic, still under-shot by Indian creators, but thin on nightlife and medical depth.

entities.name: Pai
entities.summary: 762 curves from Chiang Mai into a backpacker valley of hot springs, canyons and hammocks. The road in is the single most important attribute in the record: it is a motion-sickness generator and it prices out anyone with mobility or medical constraints.

entities.name: Hua Hin
entities.summary: The Thai royal family's seaside town: drivable from Bangkok, flat, calm, low-crime, golf courses and long shallow beaches. The strongest senior and infant profile in the country — and the weakest for anyone chasing nightlife.

entities.name: Ayutthaya
entities.summary: The UNESCO ruins of the old Siamese capital, 80 minutes from Bangkok — the country's best day-trip. Flat, cheap, heritage-dense; brutal midday heat with almost no shade, which is the single limiting factor for seniors, infants and pregnancy.

entities.name: Kanchanaburi
entities.summary: The Bridge on the River Kwai, the Death Railway, Erawan's seven-tier waterfall and floating raft houses. A heritage-plus-nature day/overnight trip from Bangkok, with a heavy emotional register and real waterfall-climbing exertion.

entities.name: Khao Lak
entities.summary: An hour north of Phuket airport: long empty beaches, big family resorts, no nightlife, and the launch point for Similan Islands liveaboards. Quiet by design — which makes it strong for infants, pregnancy and seniors, and weak for anyone under 25.

entities.name: Koh Lanta
entities.summary: The island families and remote workers choose when Phuket feels too loud: flat, car-accessible by bridge/ferry, long west-facing sunset beaches, a growing coworking scene, and prices well below Samui.

entities.name: Koh Chang
entities.summary: Thailand's second-largest island, drivable from Bangkok and still relatively unshot by Indian creators: rainforest interior, waterfalls, quiet east coast, ferry-only access and steep, hairpin internal roads.
